text:
cheng: Heads up — we're seeing a sharp latency spike on the gpt-small route in us-west1. Telemetry shows a bunch of preemptible GPUs reclaimed ~12:42 UTC.

maria: p90 token latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.1s. Errors 502 on some requests. Looks correlated with preemptible eviction events. :exclamation:

ops-bot: [alert] compute-group-us-west1-preemptible: 28 nodes reclaimed within 5m (reason: preemptible_reclaim)

tim: Is the autoscaler not moving traffic to on-demand/reserved pools?

cheng: The fallback policy kicked but client routing was sticky to the old endpoints — some frontends still had cached IPs for preemptible-only endpoints. Sticky routing + rolling evictions = partial outage for a subset of requests.

katie: I pushed a routing patch to prefer mixed-pool endpoints earlier but it didn't roll fast enough. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/3287

sarah: Trying quick mitigation: increasing reserved pool in us-west1 by 6 GPUs now. Command: `gcloud compute instances create rsvd-gpu-temp --machine-type=n1-highmem-16 --accelerator=count=2,type=nvidia-a100 --zone=us-west1-b`

maria: Also lowering serving batch size to reduce tail latency. Changing BATCH_SIZE from 4 -> 1 for gpt-small route. Doing hot config change now.

cheng: I'm adjusting autoscaler settings to be eviction-aware: reduce scale_down_grace from 600s -> 120s and add stable-pool-weight for reserved nodes so they prefer -> on-demand if preemptible capacity drains. Uploading patch in a min.

tim: Can we force DNS TTL flush on the internal LB? We need clients to stop pointing to drained endpoints.

katie: Fluent change applied: internal-lb: TTL 60 -> 15, pushed via terraform (apply id 0a7f).

ops-bot: [deploy] infra/autoscaler v2.13 deployed by katie at 12:58 UTC

cheng: Quick nugget: one of our healthcheck probes was too lenient; it allowed endpoints that were serving degraded (high queueing) to remain in rotation. Tightened probe: `initial_delay=5s, period=3s, failure_threshold=2`.

maria: Checking metrics... p90 down from 1.1s -> 220ms after reserved bump + TTL change. Error rate dropping. :thumbsup:

tim: Good. But we still need long-term: client pinning -> sticky headers need to respect fallback_policy. Add sticky-key expiry shorter than preemptible eviction window.

cheng: Agreed. Follow-ups: (1) Add eviction-aware routing rule that marks endpoints draining when cloud signals preemptible_reclaim; (2) Create alert when >10% of pool reclaimed in 5m; (3) Simulate evictions in staging to validate.

katie: I'll own (1) and (2). Putting a runbook snippet in the infra ops doc.

ops-bot: [note] Incident classified as partial-service-degradation. Postmortem owner required.

cheng: I'll draft the postmortem. Initial RCA: mixed-capacity pool + client-side sticky routing + lenient healthchecks + autoscaler scale_down_grace too long.

sarah: Cost note: reserved bump costs ~+$6k/month if kept. Recommend short-term reserve until we improve routing and then revert.

maria: For now revert batch size once stable. Leave reserved expansion on for 2 hours, then reassess.

tim: Adding action items to infra board (#infra-ops): Eviction-aware routing (katie), Healthcheck tightening (cheng), Sticky expiry change (tim), Staging evictions test (sarah).

cheng: Thanks all. Monitoring for 30m, will update thread with final status.

maria: Update: 13:18 UTC all clear for gpt-small route, p95 back to baseline. Closing immediate mitigation.

ops-bot: [resolved] compute-group-us-west1-preemptible alert cleared at 13:20 UTC

cheng: Postmortem draft will be ready EOD. Leaving this thread for follow-ups. :memo:
